title: S3/Blob Storage Growth Trending

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch` events with `Namespace="AWS/S3" MetricName="BucketSizeBytes"` into `index=cloud`. Confirm UC-4.6.4 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch` traffic without `Namespace="AWS/S3" MetricName="BucketSizeBytes"`. Confirm UC-4.6.4 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS (S3 storage metrics), Azure Monitor metrics; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Splunk Add-on for AWS (S3 storage metrics), Azure Monitor metrics
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" Namespace="AWS/S3" MetricName="BucketSizeBytes"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.4_s3_blob_storage_growth_t_4"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.6.4 — S3/Blob Storage Growth Trending: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudwatch` for search criteria `Namespace="AWS/S3" MetricName="BucketSizeBytes"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for capacity review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), detecting 'S3/Blob Storage Growth Trending' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.6.4 drives medium-priority capacity alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Ingest daily CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes per bucket or storage account metrics for Azure/Blob. Use span=1mon aligned to calendar months for FinOps reporting. Convert bytes to TB for readability. Optionally exclude archive buckets matched to a lookup. Alert on month-over-month growth above a percentage threshold. Use predict to forecast 3 months ahead for capacity planning.
visualization: Line chart (total TB monthly with 3-month forecast), bar chart (top buckets by size), table (month-over-month growth %).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.storage_free_percent) as free_pct
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.Storage
  by Performance.host span=1h
| sort 10 free_pct
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (Storage node).
knownFalsePositives: Inventories can skip a run when an API is throttled or a connector is in maintenance, which looks like a big drop. We check the ingest time and the last good snapshot before we call it shrinkage.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (S3 storage metrics), Azure Monitor metrics with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.6.7.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest daily CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes per bucket or storage account metrics for Azure/Blob. Use span=1mon aligned to calendar months for FinOps reporting. Convert bytes to TB for readability. Optionally exclude archive buckets matched to a lookup. Alert on month-over-month growth above a percentage threshold. Use predict to forecast 3 months ahead for capacity planning.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" Namespace="AWS/S3" MetricName="BucketSizeBytes"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.4_s3_blob_storage_growth_t_4"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=cloud` to detect s3/blob storage growth trending. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_6_4_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (total TB monthly with 3-month forecast), bar chart (top buckets by size), table (month-over-month growth %)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (S3 storage metrics), Azure Monitor metrics and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of s3/blob storage growth trending so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
